info.title: Options Analysis Suite API
info.description:
Institutional-grade options analytics API. Programmatic access to 17 pricing models (including 7 exotic options), auto-calibration, real-time exposure analytics, WebSocket streaming, and pre-computed market data.

## Features

- **17 pricing models** — 10 standard (Black-Scholes, Heston, SABR, FFT (Carr-Madan with 6 characteristic functions), Variance Gamma, Jump Diffusion (Kou/Bates/Merton), Binomial, PDE, Monte Carlo, Local Volatility (Dupire + eSSVI)) plus 7 exotic (Barrier, Asian, Lookback, Digital, Compound, Chooser, Multi-Asset) with optional strategy-insight card via `includeInsight`
- **Auto-calibration** — Heston, SABR, VG, JD, and Local Vol calibrate against live broker chain data in 0.25-16s
- **Greek exposure** — GEX, DEX, VEX, Vanna, Charm, Vomma under two methodologies: 1 (legacy) with gamma flip detection, call/put walls, abs gamma anchor and dealer positioning regime; 2, the assumed dealer book and Long OI over each side's bases with their coverage, served as `exposureV2` beside the legacy fields on the snapshot and end-of-day exposure endpoints, chosen per request on `/v1/compute/exposure` and per subscription on the stream
- **Real-time streaming** — WebSocket endpoint for live quotes, Greeks, and computed exposure snapshots
- **Pre-computed data** — market regime, IV surfaces, snapshots, metrics, scanner, risk-neutral + lognormal probability distributions

## Authentication

All `/v1/*` endpoints require an API key. Pass it via either header:

- `Authorization: Bearer oas_live_...`
- `X-API-Key: oas_live_...`

## Rate limits

Separate buckets for data and compute endpoints (per user, shared across all API keys):

- **Data** (`/v1/data/*`): **120 requests/minute**
- **Compute** (`/v1/compute/*`): **120 requests/minute**
- **Cheap compute**: max **6 concurrent** - `/price` and `/greeks` on BS, binomial, and the barrier, digital, compound and chooser models unless `modelParams.method` is `mc` / `montecarlo`; continuous lookback, one or two discrete fixings and the larger-than-2520-fixing lookback approximation unless Monte Carlo; exposure, max pain, expected move, and probability in `simple` mode
- **Heavy compute**: max **2 concurrent** - `/price` and `/greeks` on MC, PDE, Heston, Local Vol, SABR, JD, VG, FFT, Asian and Multi-Asset; discrete lookback with 3..2520 future fixings; and on any exotic model whose `modelParams.method` is `mc` / `montecarlo`; every scenario, sensitivity and strategy request; probability in `full` mode
- **Per-request computation**: a binomial, Heston or Local Vol request whose work would pass one request's allowance is refused before that work runs, with **422** `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (see the `modelParams` notes on `/v1/compute/price`)
- **Calibration**: max **1 concurrent** job (own lane, separate from compute pools) · hard-capped at **500/day** per user
- Heavy compute endpoints may return **503** when worker capacity is unavailable
- 429 responses include `X-RateLimit-Bucket` header (`data` or `compute`)

## Broker credentials (BYOK)

Some endpoints (calibration, full-mode probability, streaming) require live broker chain data. The API doesn't pay for market data; you supply your own credentials via request headers (the streaming endpoint takes them in its initial WebSocket auth message instead):

- **TastyTrade**: `X-Broker-Type: tastytrade`, `X-Tastytrade-Refresh-Token`, `X-Tastytrade-Client-Secret`
- **Tradier**: `X-Broker-Type: tradier`, `X-Tradier-Key`
- **Schwab**: `X-Broker-Type: schwab`, `X-Schwab-Refresh-Token`, `X-Schwab-Client-Id`, `X-Schwab-Client-Secret` (calibration, full-mode probability, and streaming; streaming additionally requires a Schwab app approved for Accounts and Trading)
- **moomoo**: `X-Broker-Type: moomoo`, `X-Moomoo-Sealed-Token` (the API token from the moomoo card on your Account page: moomoo's read-only sign-in, sealed to your account, so it works only with API keys on the account that connected moomoo; streaming takes it as `credentials.moomooSealedToken` and carries quotes, not Greeks)

Note: Public.com is **not accepted as a per-request header credential** on these endpoints, and no `/v1` endpoint reads a stored credential. A broker credential stored against your account is read by the platform's live-data routes, which sit outside `/v1` and are not part of this contract or its SDK; they are what the MCP server's live tools (`get_live_options_chain`, `get_live_dealer_positioning` and the other live tools) call. Storage is an opt-in on the account page for the Pro tier and above, and is offered for Tradier, tastytrade, Schwab, Public.com and moomoo. Public.com is also available for direct in-browser use on the Pro webapp tier.

## Best practices (especially for LLM-driven agents)

- **Calibrate once, then persist the fitted params — not the `calibrationId`.** `calibrationId` is a short-lived handle into a 30-second in-memory cache; it works for immediate follow-up `/price` and `/greeks` calls but is not durable. For reuse beyond 30s, save the fitted parameters from the calibration response and pass them as `modelParams` on subsequent calls. Either path avoids the 500/day calibration quota. Don't set `resolve.calibration: true` on every repeated call for the same symbol.
- **Prefer `/v1/data/*` over recomputing.** Greeks history, IV surfaces, snapshot metrics, metrics-batch, scanner rankings, and regime classifications are precomputed or cached where available — typically much faster than recomputing from scratch. Don't loop `/v1/compute/greeks` to reconstruct what `/v1/data/greeks-history/:symbol` already returns.
- **Use batch endpoints.** `/v1/data/metrics/batch` takes multiple symbols in one call; MultiAsset accepts `modelParams.tickers` for basket pricing. One batch call beats a loop of N single-symbol calls.
- **Use canonical ticker symbols.** Symbols may contain letters, numbers, dot, dash, or slash (examples: `SPY`, `BRK.B`, `BRK-B`, `/ES`). Space-separated class shares such as `BRK B` are rejected; use dot or dash form instead.
- **Use ticker auto-fill instead of fabricated numerics.** Pass `symbol` + `expiry` and let the API resolve `S`, `sigma`, `r`, `t` from cached market data — the response's `resolved` block shows which source filled each field (`snapshot`, `atmIv-expiry`, `hv-20d`, `fred-DGS3MO`, …). Don't hallucinate market values from training data.
- **Always inspect `warnings` and `resolved`.** The compute route returns top-level `warnings` plus a `resolved` block whenever ticker auto-fill ran. Agents that ignore these can act on a price computed with a stale spot or a missing-dividend fallback.
- **Honor `Retry-After` on 429.** Sleep the suggested duration. Retrying instantly in a tight loop wastes tokens and bounces off the same limit.
- **Use `X-Cache-Status` to guide polling cadence.** Data responses include `X-Cache-Status`; values include `HIT`, `MISS`, `DEDUP`, `NO_REDIS`, and error/fallback statuses. If you see all HITs, you're polling faster than the underlying data updates — back off.
- **Don't repoll faster than the underlying data updates.** Most `/v1/data/*` endpoints back tables that refresh on a documented daily cron. Repolling every 30s returns the same bytes.
- **Stream live data over `/v1/ws`, don't poll REST.** Up to 30 msg/sec × 50 symbols × 5 sessions beats any REST polling loop on freshness and rpm budget.
- **Match model to task.** Black-Scholes and Binomial are correct for vanilla options. Black-Scholes answers in well under a millisecond. Binomial without a discrete-dividend schedule answers in milliseconds at its default 200 steps, but its work grows with the square of `steps` and `/v1/compute/greeks` prices dozens of trees, so at 2000 steps a Greeks request takes under a second. A discrete-dividend schedule adds work (up to a few seconds), and on `CRR` and `JR` it adds trees, enough for a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` at modest step counts (see the binomial notes on `/v1/compute/price`). Raise `steps` only as far as the accuracy you need. Reserve Heston/SABR/Local Vol/JD/MC for cases where skew, jumps, or path-dependence actually matter.
- **Scope and secure keys.** Create compute-only, data-only, or streaming-only keys to limit blast radius. Never embed keys in client-side JS, browser extensions, public repos, or LLM tool manifests.

post.description:
Price an option using one of 17 supported pricing models. For advanced models, pass model-specific parameters via `modelParams`, or use a `calibrationId` from `/v1/compute/calibrate` to reuse calibrated parameters.

**Required tenor:** every request must specify a time-to-expiry. Provide either `t` (numeric years) **or** `expiry` / `expiration` (YYYY-MM-DD). Missing both returns a `400` validation error.

**Ticker auto-fill:** supply `symbol: "AAPL"` (plus `expiry: "YYYY-MM-DD"` since tenor is mandatory) to let the API fill `S`, `sigma`, `q`, `r`, and `t` from cached market data. User-supplied numeric fields always win; the response `resolved` block reports the effective value + source (`override`, `snapshot`, `atmIv-expiry`, `hv-20d`, `hv-realized-<n>obs`, `ratios_ttm`, `profile_yield`, `fred-DGS3MO`, etc.). A realized volatility computed from price history not yet confirmed by a refresh carries the suffix `-unconfirmed` (`hv-realized-<n>obs-unconfirmed`), and a MultiAsset leg whose volatility or correlation was estimated from such history adds a warning naming the ticker. For MultiAsset, supply `modelParams.tickers: ["SPY","QQQ",...]` to build the basket from 5y monthly correlations. Requires both `compute` and `data` scopes on the API key. Set `resolve.calibration: true` (Heston/SABR/VG/JD/LocalVol only) to additionally run auto-calibration under the existing calibration quota — broker headers (`X-Broker-Type`, `X-Tradier-Key`, …) are required for this mode.

**modelParams by model:**

- **heston:** `v0` / `initialVariance` / `hestonV0`, `kappa` / `hestonKappa`, `theta` / `hestonTheta`, `volOfVol` / `sigmaV` / `hestonXi` / `xi` / `hestonVolOfVol` (legacy alias: `sigma`), `rho` / `hestonRho`, `integrationPoints` (legacy alias: `hestonOrder`). Every spelling listed here is accepted identically on `/price`, `/greeks` and `/sensitivity`. Omitted parameters take these defaults, which materially affect the price: `v0` = `sigma^2`, `theta` = `sigma^2`, `kappa` = 2.0, `volOfVol` = 0.3, `rho` = -0.7. Supply them explicitly (or via a calibration) rather than relying on the defaults. Domain rules, applied identically on `/price`, `/greeks` and `/sensitivity` and rejected with a 422 `INVALID_HESTON_PARAMS`: `v0 >= 0`, `theta >= 0` (both are variances), `kappa > 0` (a mean-reversion speed), `volOfVol >= 0`, and `-1 < rho < 1` strictly. Every one of these parameters must be a number or a numeric string; booleans, arrays and objects are rejected with a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` rather than coerced. `integrationPoints` is the exception to the last rule only in range: a value outside 8..128 is clamped into it rather than rejected. It no longer changes the price: the Fourier integration follows the characteristic function (its range and its subdivision adapt to it), so it is accepted for compatibility only. A contract whose integration does not settle (a correlation near -1 or 1 with almost no variance to expiry) is rejected with a 422 `NON_FINITE_RESULT` rather than priced: on `/price`; on `/greeks` when the price or any price its Greeks are differenced from does not settle; and on `/sensitivity` when the price or a model derivative at any point does not. One request may spend at most 8 million Fourier integrand evaluations: each panel of the integration (15 evaluations) is charged before it is integrated, and the panel that would pass the allowance is refused with a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, so a refused request has spent at most 8 million. A `/price` or `/greeks` request fits (the Greeks take 26 integrals of at most about 100,000 evaluations each); a `/sensitivity` sweep takes eleven integrals at each of its points (an ordinary 200-point sweep spends 0.3 to 1.4 million; a correlation near -1 can need many times that), so fewer points will fit. Where a canonical spelling and a legacy alias are both supplied, the canonical one wins (`volOfVol` over `sigma`, `integrationPoints` over `hestonOrder`). On `/v1/compute/greeks`, the volatility Greeks (`vega`, `vomma`, `vanna`, `veta`, `zomma`, `ultima`, `dcharmDvol`) are taken with respect to the model`s own instantaneous volatility `sqrt(v0)`, not the request `sigma`. With `v0` omitted the two coincide, since `v0` then defaults to `sigma^2`. Note that `sigma` stops influencing the Heston price only once BOTH `v0` and `theta` are supplied - supplying `v0` alone leaves `theta` defaulting to `sigma^2`, so `sigma` still moves the price through the long-run variance (with `v0` = 0.09 and `theta` omitted, `sigma` of 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.4 prices 9.4348 / 10.8509 / 15.0789).
- **sabr:** `sabrAlpha` / `alpha`, `sabrBeta` / `beta`, `sabrRho` / `rho`, `sabrNu` / `nu`, `approximationMethod` (hagan | obloj | paulot, default hagan), `shift`, `expansionOrder`, `useSmallTimeCorrection`, `fixBeta`, `fixedBetaValue`, `atmReference`, `volFloor`, `useArbitrageChecks`
- **fft:** `processType` (blackScholes | merton | varianceGamma | heston | kou | bates), `N`, `alpha`, `eta`, `integrationMethod` (legacy aliases: `fftGridSize`, `fftAlpha`, `fftEta`, `fftIntegrationMethod`). Process-specific params match the webapp: Merton `mertonLambda`, `mertonMuJ`, `mertonSigmaJ`; Variance Gamma `vgSigma`, `vgNu`, `vgTheta`; Heston `hestonV0`, `hestonKappa`, `hestonTheta`, `hestonXi`, `hestonRho`; Kou `kouLambda`, `kouP`, `kouEta1`, `kouEta2`; Bates `batesV0`, `batesKappa`, `batesTheta`, `batesSigmaV`, `batesRho`, `batesLambda`, `batesMuJ`, `batesSigmaJ`. Single-strike Black-Scholes, Merton, Kou, Heston and Bates prices and Greeks use inversion at the requested strike, with analytic derivatives, rather than interpolation between FFT strike nodes. Black-Scholes uses its closed forms. The grid controls remain accepted and apply to full FFT surfaces, Variance Gamma and scalar inversion that does not settle within the integration limit. At positive tenor, time differences on that fallback use the smaller of one calendar day and one twentieth of the time left, centred on the requested tenor.
- **vg:** `sigma` / `vgSigma`, `nu` / `vgNu`, `theta` / `vgTheta`, optional `method`, `fftPoints`, `alpha`, `eta`, `cacheFFT`, `weighting`
- **jd:** `modelType` / `jdModel` (kou | merton | bates, default kou; any other value is rejected with a 422 rather than falling back to kou). Merton/Kou accept `baseVolatility` as the diffusion sigma override. Kou: `lambda`, `pUp`, `etaUp`, `etaDown`, optional `tailTolerance` / `tailTol`, `maxK`, `forceFFT`, `fftGridSize`. Merton: `lambda`, `muJ`, `sigmaJ`, optional `maxK` / `maxPoisson` and `tailTolerance` / `tailTol`. Its compensated Poisson series bounds both the cash and asset-weighted omitted masses by `tailTol` (default 1e-12, clamped to 1e-12 through 1e-2). The term count adapts to both Poisson means, with a default ceiling of 512 including the zero-jump term. An explicit term limit is a hard cap, clamped to 1 through 512; a series that cannot settle within it returns 422 NON_FINITE_RESULT rather than a truncated price. Bates: `v0`, `kappa`, `theta`, `sigmaV` / `volOfVol` / `xi`, `rho`, `lambda`, `muJ`, `sigmaJ`, optional `forceExactCF`, `fftGridSize`. Jump defaults when omitted: `lambda` = 0.1, `muJ` = -0.05, `sigmaJ` = 0.15, `pUp` = 0.5, `etaUp` = `etaDown` = 10. The default `maxK` is 30 for Kou and 512 for Merton. Kou uses its double-exponential jumps and Bates its Heston variance with lognormal jumps on both /price and the base of /greeks. The historical series and FFT-selection options remain accepted but do not select an approximate law for a settled single-strike calculation. At lambda = 0, Kou and Merton use Black-Scholes, including zero diffusion, and Bates uses Heston. Bates volatility Greeks vary sqrt(v0) with the other resolved parameters, including theta, fixed. With S = K = 100, r = 0.05, q = 0, sigma = 0.2 and six hours left, default Kou and Bates calls read 0.21086071 and 0.21092536, with theta -0.42578484 and -0.42603409 per calendar day.
- **binomial:** `steps`, `enableAmerican` / `isAmerican`, `treeType` (CRR | JR | LR, default LR), optional Richardson controls `useRichardsonExtrap`, `richardsonMode`, `stepMultiplier`, `extrapOrder`, and discrete-dividend inputs either as `dividends` array or the webapp-style `useDiscreteDividends`, `exDividendDates`, `dividendAmounts`. The public API uses the ex-date discrete-dividend model. With a discrete dividend, `theta` and the time cross-Greeks (`charm`, `veta`, `color`, `dcharmDvol`) are taken in calendar time: the valuation date moves, the expiry and every ex-date coming nearer together, so a payment keeps its distance to expiry. A schedule lists at most 260 payments (`dividends`, or each of `exDividendDates` and `dividendAmounts`); a longer one is rejected with a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` rather than truncated. A schedule that moves the stock further below the nodes of a tree than one tree may carry (10 million nodes below the natural bottoms of its levels, all levels together: a payment large against the node spacing of the volatility, 50 paid after a day on a stock at 100, a volatility of 0.01, 30 days, 2000 steps) is rejected with a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` rather than priced on fewer nodes; fewer `steps` need fewer, and `/v1/compute/greeks`, whose finite differences price larger trees, can reject a schedule `/v1/compute/price` accepts. One request's trees may take at most 500 million nodes of lattice work (a read between two nodes counted as 32): each tree is charged before it is built, and the tree that would pass the allowance is refused with a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`, so a refused request has done at most that much. `/v1/compute/greeks` prices dozens of trees (45 on `LR` at 2000 steps without a payment: 90 million nodes) and on `CRR` and `JR` as many more for each payment dated between two steps of a tree, so frequent schedules on those trees can exhaust the allowance at modest step counts (a year of weekly payments from about 40 steps, refused at 50 for calls and puts of either style; a year of monthly payments answered at 1000 steps and refused at 2000), depending on where the dates fall between the steps, while the default `LR`, which pays each payment on a step, fits (a year of weekly payments at 2000 steps). The trees of a `/v1/compute/scenario` matrix, of a `/v1/compute/sensitivity` sweep and of every leg of a `/v1/compute/strategy` request share one allowance (refused: a 20 by 20 matrix at 2000 steps, a 200-point sweep at 2000 steps with Richardson extrapolation, a sixth `LR` leg at 2000 steps); fewer `steps` need less. `steps` and `enableAmerican` / `isAmerican` are also accepted as top-level request fields; where both are supplied the `modelParams` spelling wins, because the generated SDKs populate the top-level pair with their own defaults even when the caller never set them. `treeType` selects the lattice construction: `CRR` is the textbook Cox-Ross-Rubinstein lattice. Its drift consumes lattice variance even when the probability is valid: for a small drift share k = |r - q - sigma^2/2| sqrt(T / steps) / sigma the lattice keeps about 1 - k^2 of the log variance, and a forward put loses about k^2/2 of its value; at a 1% volatility, a 10% rate, five years and 2000 steps it reads 13.41% below Black-Scholes (k = 0.5). The API checks every actual price tree before building it, including Greek points, aligned-node trees, Richardson pairs and strategy legs. If its final CRR or JR probability is below 0 or above 1, it refuses with 422 `INVALID_BINOMIAL_PROBABILITY` instead of using a clamped probability; exact 0 and 1 remain accepted. The message gives the smallest unclamped step count up to the 2000-step limit, or says that none exists, and recommends LR. For a valid price tree, Greek stencils stay inside its probability domain: a one-sided volatility, rate or yield stencil replaces a neighbouring stencil whose trees would require clamping. The requested price tree is unchanged; this preserves availability but does not remove the lattice drift error or certify Greek accuracy near the bound. Fewer steps cannot repair this drift problem; use more steps or LR; `JR` keeps equal-magnitude CRR up/down factors (`u·d = 1`) and puts drift into the risk-neutral probability (this is NOT the equal-probability Jarrow-Rudd 1983 tree, which puts drift into `u`/`d` with `p = 1/2` and breaks finite-difference cross-Greeks because `u·d ≠ 1`); `JR` is not an exact stock martingale: at a 20% rate, 20% volatility, five years and 50 steps its in-the-money call reads 1.48% below Black-Scholes. Coarse high-volatility wings can be worse (S 130, K 100, rate -20%, yield 10%, volatility 100%, ten years, 25 steps: 14.35 for 31.16). The native CRR and JR lattice constructions remain unchanged where their probabilities are valid; the cash-derivative refinements below are separate. `LR` is Leisen-Reimer with Peizer-Pratt inversion method 2 (with a discrete dividend, inverted at the moneyness at expiry: the spot against the strike plus the value of the payments then, moved back toward the money where its d2 falls under -4, along a smooth ramp toward -5: up to the moneyness of the spot itself in full and past it by the share 1 - e^-m of the rest, m the move of the payments in units of sigma sqrt(T), so with a small payment a spot deep in the wing keeps near its own; an American call, which with a positive rate and no continuous yield is exercised only just before a payment, at the spot itself), is the DEFAULT when `treeType` is omitted. Only where its inversion degenerates, its fallback uses reciprocal wings with log spacing sqrt(sigma^2 dt + (r - q)^2 dt^2) and the martingale probability (a deep call at S 100, K 1e-8, rate 10%, volatility 1%, five years and 200 requested steps reads 100 rather than 82.7527); the own LR lattice is unchanged. It rounds an even `steps` UP to the next odd count, except at the public 2000-step ceiling where up is unavailable so it rounds DOWN to 1999 (same rule the engine applies at its own higher MAX_BINOMIAL_STEPS). `exDividendDates` entries may be given in YEARS or in DAYS to the ex-date, and a bare number cannot say which - `2.5` on a 3-year option is a legitimate 2.5 days and a legitimate 2.5 years, and the two price differently. Set `dividendTimeUnit` (alias `exDividendTimeUnit`) to `days` or `years` to say which; any other value is rejected with a 422. When it is omitted the legacy rule applies unchanged: entries greater than 2 are read as DAYS, entries of 2 or less as YEARS. Under either reading, an entry that falls after expiry is dropped because it cannot affect the price. Without a cash schedule, Greek accuracy on the default `LR`: `delta`, `vega`, `rho`, `vanna`, `vomma` and `ultima` match Black-Scholes to better than 0.05% at the money, and `theta`, `charm`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` to better than 0.15%. `gamma` converges from 1.13% at 50 steps to 0.04% at 1600. `speed`, `zomma` and `color` are the loosest, measured 28.4%, 6.7% and 7.0% at 50 steps, 7.7%, 1.5% and 1.6% at the default 200, and 0.96%, -0.02% and 0.01% at 1600; raise `steps` when the third-order Greeks matter. Away from the money the worst of the seventeen at 200 steps is `zomma` at 20.4%, then `speed` at 9.2% and `color` at 8.9%, with everything else inside 1.2%. Accuracy degrades at low volatility, where these Greeks are also small in absolute terms.

  **`CRR` and `JR` take their Greeks off trees that share the nodes of the lattice.** Cox-Ross-Rubinstein centres its lattice on SPOT with `u·d = 1`, so a node lands on the strike only where the spot is a whole number of node spacings from it; a bumped reprice at the same step count moves the kink of the payoff between the nodes, and a finite difference across it measures that motion rather than the option (at K=100, sigma=0.2, 200 steps, `vanna` read about -0.095 whether the true value is +1.43 at S=80 or -0.96 at S=120). The stencil therefore keeps the node spacing: the spot points are whole node spacings apart, a vol bump is a change of step count at the same spacing (the time level the own steps of each tree), each payment on the own step of each tree (one between two steps read on the trees paying it on each, blended), the derivatives Fornberg weights on those points; `vomma` and `ultima` without cash, and for American calls with cash, follow the path that keeps the place of the kink of the payoff between the nodes (the strike, plus a payment at expiry; for an American call with a payment at expiry the strike or the strike plus the payment, whichever reads four times smoother along its path by the fourth differences of the price over the vol steps (a kink crossing a node reads as a corner), else the strike plus the payment under the rate step K (e^(r dt) - 1) and the strike from it, the strike alone where every payment is on the last step or between it and the one before, the rate is not negative and each tree of the blend pays on each of those two steps nothing, or at least the rate step and more than K (e^h - 1) at every vol read (the holder then exercises the step before each payment wherever in the money), the vol steps about the vol unless those on one side read four times smoother where the payment nears the continuation at the strike, K (e^h - 1) with h the node spacing, or lies between it and the rate step when every payment is on the last step or between it and the one before and the rate is not negative (the trees price no yield beside a cash payment), fourth differences under the rounding of the trees (16 eps (n P + sqrt(n) (S + K)), P the largest price read, and 16 eps n S more on JR) reading as that rounding, the vol step 0.001 or a twentieth of a vol under 0.02; the spot moving with the vol bump, the spot terms taken back out by the chain rule), `ultima` blending into the trees sharing the nodes beyond a kink 0.75 to 1.25 sigma sqrt(t) away. With cash, European calls and puts and American puts at a nonpositive rate instead integrate the continuous cash-date conditional expectations, including the stock floor at zero. Positive-rate American puts instead fit nine full continuous-exercise PDE prices over a volatility band no wider than a twentieth of the requested volatility. Each solve moves the exercise boundary; the default auxiliary mesh has 950 intervals and its resolution does not increase with `steps`. A translated put width not fully represented on the default mesh may use an additional 1900-interval fit, after all initial curvature fits have finished. The same continuous resolution weights apply on each mesh, and the finer fit refines only the remaining native share. A budget refusal or coded accuracy failure retains the completed earlier pair with a short notice; a declined finer method retains it silently. It retains spatial and volatility-band error: against independent continuous-exercise references over 63 cash-put contracts, the worst scaled error is 2.5% in `vomma` and 36% in `ultima` (scaled by the greater of the reference magnitude and 1). Where a uniform bound makes the fitted exercise premium negligible, the conditional European values are retained. A pass with an unrepresentable grid, unresolved cash-shifted payoff width or unresolved contact retains the previous completed estimate. An eligible later finer mesh can still refine its native share. A cash-shifted payoff width covered by four to eight auxiliary cells transitions continuously between native and fitted estimates; eight cells take the fitted value. This resolution rule does not certify either estimate. Every mandatory native calculation for the whole request completes before the auxiliary solves and conditional integrals use the remaining computation budget, including every option leg of a strategy. A budget refusal or coded accuracy failure retains the last completed estimate of the affected Greeks with a short `warnings` notice; for an initial curvature fit this is the native `vomma` and `ultima`. A declined method can retain the estimate silently. This preserves availability without certifying the retained values. Attempted auxiliary work remains charged. The published price retains the requested tree. On LR, cash `vomma` and `ultima` for European options and American puts use these same conditional or continuous-exercise calculations; American calls retain their existing LR stencils. LR cash `speed` and calendar `dcharmDvol` also differentiate the conditional density for a European option or a nonpositive-rate American put with at most one positive pre-terminal cash date, with any terminal cash paid in the payoff; other cases retain the native spatial and time-vol stencils. Optional LR work follows the previously funded CRR and JR fits, and additional spatial work follows all cash-curvature fits. Against Black-Scholes over 336 cells (S 80 to 120, vols 0.1 to 0.6, 2 days to a year, 200 steps), the worst error: `vega` 0.7%, `vanna` 3.1%, `zomma` 3.3%, `speed` 3.7%, `theta` 4.8%, `veta` 5.8%, `charm` 10.2%, `dcharmDvol` 22.8%, `vomma` 23.9%, `ultima` 55% (JR 22%), the medians under 1.7%; with one cash dividend (240 European cells, calendar time) `vega` 0.7%, `vanna` 2.0%, `zomma` 5.0%, `speed` 2.8%, `veta` 1.4%, `theta` 3.0%, `charm` 6.1%, `vomma` 0.000002%, `dcharmDvol` 16.7% (24 cells over 10%), and `ultima` 0.000014% at worst on both spot-centred trees (no `vomma` or `ultima` cell over 10%). `CRR` price, `delta`, `gamma` and `rho` are the own values of the tree, as before; `theta` comes off the trees sharing the nodes too (the native step at the held count respaced them: 33.7% at worst over the 336 cells). The default `LR` pins a node on the strike and stays the better lattice for the cross-Greeks without a dividend (`vanna` 1.5%, `vomma` 0.7% on the 336 cells); with one, the conditional LR values over the same 240 cells read `vomma` 0.000002% and `ultima` 0.000014% at worst, `dcharmDvol` 0.027% and `speed` 0.012%, with no cell over 10% in those four fields (own-date conditional quadrature, calendar time; its finite-difference references also retain numerical error); `CRR` is retained because it is the canonical textbook construction that callers cross-check against, and `JR` shares its `u·d = 1` geometry.
- **pde:** `forceMethod` / `pdeForceMethod` (`analytical` | `pde` | `pde-with-fallback`, normalized case-insensitively; unsupported values return 422), `accuracyThreshold` / `pdeAccuracyThreshold` (non-negative; malformed or negative values return 422), plus grid controls `spaceSteps`, `timeSteps`, `sMin`, `sMax`, `gridSpacing`, `rannacherSteps`. Default grids cover spot and strike with diffusion-scaled bounds and place the payoff kink between uniform nodes. Supplied bounds retain their requested width; a spot outside those bounds returns analytical pricing. European boundary values include time value. The time cross-Greeks and enhanced theta use the last three solve levels on the same grid; native theta uses the PDE identity. Theta uses a 365-day year before the requested dayCount scaling. Each Rannacher interval uses two implicit half steps before Crank-Nicolson. A requested rannacherSteps value of 1 uses two startup intervals to damp time cross-Greek ringing; values of 2 or more use the requested count. The requested timeSteps count is unchanged. Zero Rannacher steps use a second-order stiffly stable two-stage method to suppress oscillatory curvature. Ultima differences cell-averaged out-of-the-money parity payoffs to avoid intrinsic-value rounding and kink-phase error, cancels the leading volatility-step error and extrapolates two uniform auxiliary spatial meshes with the same bounds and time steps. The auxiliary coarse count is the smaller of the requested count and 2048, the fine count twice that, within the same 4096-interval cap. A nonuniform request keeps that geometry for its price and every other Greek; only ultima uses the uniform auxiliary meshes. The existing accuracy checks and analytical fallback remain in force; the additional Greeks carry the existing not-certified warning
- **mc:** `paths` / `mcPaths` / `nPaths`, `steps` / `stepsPerPath` / `timeSteps` / `nSteps`, `seed` / `mcSeed`, `process` / `processType` (`blackscholes` | `jumpdiffusion` | `meanreverting` | `heston` | `localvolcev` | `localvoldupire`; aliases such as `BlackScholes`, `Merton`, `LocalVolatility`, `Dupire`, and `CEV` are normalized), top-level process params or nested `processParams`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`, `useImportanceSampling`, `useMomentMatching`, `useQMC`, `qmcType` (`sobol` | `halton`; other values return 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM`). `processType`, `qmcType`, and `rngMethod` must be strings when supplied; arrays, booleans, and objects return 422 rather than being string-coerced. `rngMethod: SobolTrue` is normalized to Sobol QMC; non-QMC browser RNG labels fall back to the standard server RNG path. Monte Carlo pricing in the API is European-only. On `/price` and on the base price of `/greeks`, a sampled price is refused with 422 `MC_PRICE_UNRESOLVED` when the price plus three reported standard errors lies below the European lower bound by more than `1e-6 * S`: `max(S exp(-q t) - K exp(-r t), 0)` for a call, its mirror for a put. The mean-reverting process is exempt because its law does not use that risk-neutral forward. Missing or non-finite standard error alone does not cause this refusal. The message gives the price, standard error and bound, and advises more paths, a shorter tenor or the analytical model. This screen detects some unresolved samples; passing it does not certify sample accuracy. Browser-only execution flags such as `useGPU`, `batchSize`, and `parallelThreads` are ignored server-side. Nested `processParams` may supply process-specific fields but cannot override the validated request coordinates `S`, `r`, `q`, `sigma`, or `T`. QMC dimension is the path step count: Sobol supports at most 40 `nSteps` and Halton at most 10. A larger value (including the 252-step non-GBM default when `nSteps` is omitted) returns a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` rather than silently running the pseudo-random path or surfacing a generator error.

  `seed` / `mcSeed` is validated rather than coerced: it must be an integer with `|seed| < 2^52` and must not be 0. Zero is rejected because the engine builds its generator with `seed || Date.now()`, so a zero seed silently becomes the wall clock - and on `/v1/compute/greeks` the seed is reused across every bumped evaluation to give common random numbers, so a wall-clock seed would make each bump draw a different stream and the Greeks would measure Monte Carlo noise rather than the bump. Fractional, out-of-range, non-numeric and array/boolean/object values return a `422` with `code: "INVALID_MODEL_PARAM"`; a numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer (`"1337"` yes, `"1.5"` no). On the standard pseudo-random path the generator reduces the seed to 32 bits, so seeds differing by a multiple of 2^32 are the same seed. That equivalence does NOT extend to the QMC paths (`useQMC` with Sobol or Halton): those initializers scale the raw seed before reducing it, and above 2^53 / 1664525 the multiply loses precision, so two seeds a multiple of 2^32 apart diverge - a call at S = K = 100 (r 0.05, q 0.02, a vol of 0.2, a year), 1,000 paths of 8 steps without the control variate, prices 9.3201 vs 9.3904 under Sobol and 9.4955 vs 9.2343 under Halton at seeds 1 and 1 + 1000x2^32, against an identical 9.0763 on the standard path. Repeating the same seed is deterministic on every path, and on every supported `processType`. With a valid seed, repeating a request returns the identical price.
  Two of the six processes carry their own instantaneous-volatility input: `heston` reads `v0` (the instantaneous variance, aliased `hestonV0`; where both spellings are present `hestonV0` wins, matching the process itself) and `meanreverting` reads `meanRevertSigma`. Either may be a number or a non-blank numeric string; accepted strings are normalized before pricing so `/price` and `/greeks` use the same value. Supplied non-numeric, blank, or negative values return a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` on both endpoints rather than being quietly replaced. Heston permits the valid boundary `v0 = 0`; mean-reverting requires `meanRevertSigma > 0` because its engine treats zero as omission. A request-level `sigma = 0` is likewise preserved rather than defaulted to 0.2, and omitted Heston `v0` / `theta` then derive as zero. Explicit Heston `theta = 0` and `sigmaV = 0` are also preserved rather than replaced by their defaults.
  On `/v1/compute/greeks`, the volatility Greeks (`vega`, `vanna`, `vomma`, `veta`, `zomma`, `ultima`, `dcharmDvol`) are differentiated with respect to whichever state the process actually reads: `sqrt(v0)` for Heston (matching the semi-analytic `heston` model), `meanRevertSigma` for mean-reverting, an additive parallel local-volatility shift for a supplied fitted Dupire surface, and request `sigma` for the other processes. For a supplied fitted surface the shift is centered at zero and matches the localvol PDE convention: request sigma neither anchors the fit nor rescales its base law. Prebuilt Dupire grids retain their proportional sigma/reference convention; supplied local-volatility functions retain their direct values without request-sigma scaling. The constrained-slice representation and fit policy stay fixed across one Greek stencil. Supplied observations are refit at bumped spot, rate and yield; fit warnings describe only the base fit. With explicit Heston `v0`, only that state moves and request `sigma` stays fixed, so an omitted long-run variance `theta` remains at the value `/price` derived from request `sigma`. With `v0` omitted, the stencil rewrites its implicit `v0 = sigma^2`; an implicit `theta = sigma^2` moves with it, preserving the pre-existing derivative coordinate. The scaled step keeps ordinary positive values in range. At `v0 = 0`, and at request `sigma = 0` for the remaining magnitude-volatility processes, the centered stencil uses the even continuation in volatility rather than sending a negative magnitude to the engine. A supplied fitted Dupire surface instead reads signed additive shifts around its fitted local volatility, including when request sigma is zero. A positive value so small that the second- or third-order finite-difference denominator underflows can still be priced, but `/greeks` returns a 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` instead of publishing sanitized zero derivatives.
- **localvol:** PDE-only public surface. Supported params: `impliedVolData` (array or JSON string), `impliedVolDataArray`, `useDupire`, `useAmerican`, `interpolation` (essvi | linear | svi | dupire; cubic is no longer supported), `spotSteps` / `pdeGridSize`, `timeSteps` / `pdeTimeSteps`, `rannacherSteps`, `regularizationParam`, `localVolBeta` / `beta` / `cevBeta`, `cevScale`, `minVol` / `dupireMinVol`, `maxVol` / `dupireMaxVol`, `ticker`. `essvi` is the default surface fit: deterministic confidence-weighted Huber fitting in implied-volatility units per maturity, constrained SSVI slices, and a monotone total-variance clock. The Huber cutoff is 0.003 in decimal implied volatility; quote confidence multiplies the loss once. Request sigma and focus hints do not anchor supplied observations. Before the first maturity, variance starts from zero; past the last, theta continues at its final slope with fixed wing parameters. When the constrained slice fit misses any usable node by more than 0.001 in absolute implied volatility, warnings give the measured residual and the constrained slice fit is retained. Residual warnings remain informational through the 0.003 Huber scale; fit quality degrades above that scale or above 0.02 implied-volatility RMSE. Maturities with fewer than three distinct strikes constrain variance levels only; they borrow smile shape from identified maturities, or use an explicitly diagnosed flat convention when no skew is identified. Grid fits remain available only by explicit interpolation selection. No fixed global eight-parameter family is imposed on a supplied surface. The names `linear`, `svi` and `dupire` select the same regularized total-variance grid fit, not separate linear or SVI models; `regularizationParam: 0` leaves its implied vols unsmoothed. Grid nodes accept `T` / `time` / `maturity` in years or `dte` / `daysToExpiry` / `days_to_expiry` in days (365.25 a year), `K` / `strike`, and `sigma` / `vol` / `iv` / `impliedVol` / `impliedVolatility`; a finite numeric `price` is inverted to its European implied vol at the request `r` and `q` before fitting. For price nodes, side precedence is `isCall`, then `isPut` (negated), then the first non-null value of `optionType` / `option_type` / `type` / `right` / `callPut` / `call_put`. The selected flag must be boolean (null also drops the node); a selected name must be `c`, `call`, `calls`, `p`, `put` or `puts`, ignoring case and surrounding whitespace. An invalid selected value drops the node; later fields are ignored. With no side the price is a call. Nodes without a finite numeric price ignore side metadata. Invalid nodes are dropped and counted, duplicate strikes are merged by mean total variance, and a maturity needs three distinct strikes. Forward variance is the slope between its bracketing slices, starts from zero total variance, and continues at the last interval slope after the final slice. For this grid fit the PDE integrates bounded local variance within each time step, splitting at the surface maturities without adding time levels. Where local variance is invalid, the fit uses the positive slice implied vol and reports the count in warnings, with how many valid evaluations lie beyond the supplied strike range of at least one active maturity slice at fixed forward log-moneyness; invalid-input fallbacks have no spatial classification. If no grid fit can be built, the request is refused with 422 `LOCAL_VOL_FIT_FAILED`; the message carries the fit reason and dropped-point or slice diagnostics, and advises finite positive vols at three distinct strikes in at least one maturity. A supplied, non-null surface that the default eSSVI fit cannot use is refused with the same code, including malformed containers and empty arrays. A usable fit keeps its diagnostic warnings. The MC Dupire process also refuses a supplied surface it cannot fit instead of substituting CEV. Without implied vol data the local vol is CEV, `cevScale * (S / S0)^(localVolBeta - 1)`, normalized at the request's spot `S0` so every strike is priced under one process; `cevScale` defaults to `sigma`. `spotSteps` / `pdeGridSize` (the spot grid's steps, default 200) and `timeSteps` / `pdeTimeSteps` (the fewest time steps a solve takes, default 100) are clamped into 25..1800, and with `useDupire` or implied vol data each is at least 361. A solve takes more time steps where the maturity or the grid's spacing needs them, but never more than 1800, however long the maturity. One request may solve at most 45 million cells (a solve's grid nodes times its time steps, plus the nodes of each exercise pass an American solve takes past three a step): each solve, and each such pass, is charged before it runs, and the one that would pass the allowance is refused with a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`. A solve on the largest grid (1801 nodes by 1800 steps) is 3.2 million cells; `/v1/compute/greeks` solves 8 or 9 times on the request's grid, and more, up to 37, where its vol bumps reach a `minVol` / `maxVol` clamp or the exercise boundary at the spot (the bumps are then taken on one side or halved), so on the largest grid it is refused past 13 solves; a coarser grid fits more.
- **barrier:** `barrierType` (up-out | down-out | up-in | down-in | double-out | double-in), `barrierLevel`, `rebate`, `monitoringType` / `monitoring` (continuous | discrete), `monitoringFrequency` / `monitoringFreq` / `observationFreq`, `monitoringDates`, `upperBarrier`, `lowerBarrier`, `upperRebate`, `lowerRebate`. Window monitoring and its `windowStart` / `windowEnd` range are unsupported; choosing `window` returns 422 `INVALID_BARRIER_MONITORING`. Discrete frequency is a finite positive annual rate (number or numeric string), default 252; the future fixing count is `max(1, round(frequency * t))`. Named frequency aliases daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly mean 252, 52, 12, 4 per year. Canonical frequency wins over aliases. Optional `monitoringDates` takes precedence over frequency and must be a nonempty strictly increasing numeric array of uniformly spaced future year fractions ending at expiry; CSV days and irregular schedules return 422 `INVALID_BARRIER_MONITORING`. Current spot is excluded from discrete fixings, so touching a barrier at valuation does not establish a past hit. One future fixing uses the exact terminal lognormal law; hit and expiry rebates then both pay at expiry. Two or more fixings use the Broadie-Glasserman-Kou continuity approximation and return a warning on prices and Greeks: sparse monitoring and barriers close to spot can have material approximation error, and hit rebates use the approximated continuous hitting time. Greek time bumps hold the resolved fixing count fixed.
- **asian:** `averagingType` (arithmetic | geometric), `strikeType` (fixed | floating), `method` (curran | geometric; `mc`/`montecarlo` requests are normalized to curran server-side), `numObservations` (omitted and zero use the pricer's `floor(252 * t)` default - `ASIAN_DEFAULTS` carries `0`, so zero does not mean "one fixing"; positive values truncate toward zero, a result below 1 retains the zero/default behavior, and the effective count clamps to 1..2048; negative, non-finite, empty, boolean, array and object values return 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM`), `observationFreq`, `observationDates` (array or JSON-encoded array of future times to each fixing in years from the valuation time; it must contain at least one date, and dates must be finite, positive, strictly increasing and no later than `t`; malformed/non-array/empty values, violations of those rules, and schedules over 2048 entries return 422 rather than silently using or truncating the generated schedule. On `/greeks`, elapsed finite-difference time is subtracted from every date, explicit or derived, preserving the calendar spacing; the step is shortened when needed so it cannot pass the first fixing. An omitted schedule is materialized once at the requested tenor and then shifted the same way, so the time Greeks measure the decay of the position held rather than a family of contracts re-specified at each bumped tenor; this can change time Greeks materially compared with the old rescaled-schedule behavior. `observationDates` now also applies to `averagingType: "arithmetic"`, which previously derived its schedule from `(t, numObservations)` alone and ignored the parameter; where a schedule is supplied its length defines the future fixing count, matching the geometric path), `pastFixings`, `runningAverage`, `runningSum`, `fixingsElapsed`. `fixingDates` and `observations` are accepted aliases for the observation COUNT, not for a schedule; passing an array to either returns 422
- **lookback:** `lookbackType` (floating | fixed), `currentMax`, `currentMin`, `monitoringType` / `monitoring`, `monitoringFrequency`, `method`. Prices use a normal CDF accurate to double precision; time Greeks hold the rounded fixing count from the request tenor across the time stencil. Discrete monitoring uses the actual future fixing law for 1..2520 fixings, with the current spot excluded and the terminal spot included; larger counts retain a continuity approximation. Continuous spot Greeks hold the running record after the base spot is observed. One request may spend at most 4 billion transition-equivalent multiply-adds on discrete record construction and floating moments. Each distinct law and record side is charged once per request, even when cached, before its arrays and transition work; strike sweeps reuse that charge. A law that would exceed the remaining allowance is refused with 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`; fewer future fixings or fewer legs need less. Insight scenario reprices share the primary request allowance. Discrete monitoring at 3..2520 future fixings uses the heavy concurrency lane; continuous monitoring, one or two fixings and the larger-count approximation stay cheap unless a Monte Carlo method is requested.
- **digital:** `type` / `digitalType` — accepts either short form (`cash` | `asset` | `gap`) or long form (`cash-or-nothing` | `asset-or-nothing` | `gap`); both are equivalent server-side. Also `cashAmount`, `gapAmount`, `smoothing` (clamped server-side to a minimum of 1e-4), `method`
- **compound:** `compoundType` (call-on-call | call-on-put | put-on-call | put-on-put), `underlyingStrike`, `firstExpiry`, `secondExpiry` (defaults to request `t`), `method`, `mcPaths`, `mcSeed`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`. Requires 0 < `firstExpiry` < `secondExpiry`; violations are rejected with a 422 on both `/price` and `/greeks`. A supplied `mcPaths` is clamped to 2..1000000; when it is omitted the pricer applies its own default of **10000** paths, so omitting it is not the same as sending 100000. The lower bound is 2 rather than 1 because the antithetic path pairs `floor(mcPaths / 2)` draws, and a single path yields none. `mcSeed` does not clamp: it must be an integer with `|mcSeed| < 2^52` and must not be 0 (the pricer reads `mcSeed || Date.now()`, so a zero seed would silently become the wall clock). Fractional, out-of-range, non-numeric and array/boolean/object values are rejected with a 422. A numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer: `"1337"` yes, `"1.0000000000000001"` no. Two limits worth knowing rather than discovering. First, the seed is reduced to 32 bits by the generator, so seeds differing by a multiple of 2^32 are the same seed. Second, a JSON number literal is rounded to a double by the parser before the API ever sees it, so a fraction finer than the double spacing at your magnitude is already gone and no server-side check can recover it - `1.0000000000000001` arrives as `1`. That is why seeds at or above 2^52 are refused outright (there the spacing reaches 1, so any fractional literal has already become an integer), and why the string form is the exact one at every magnitude.
- **chooser:** `chooserType` (simple | complex; anything else is a 422), `choiceTime`, `maturity`, `callStrike`, `putStrike`, `callMaturity`, `putMaturity`, `method`, `mcPaths`, `rngSeed` / `seed` / `mcSeed`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`. `choiceTime` must be positive. A **simple** chooser additionally requires `maturity` > `choiceTime`; a **complex** chooser requires `callMaturity` > `choiceTime` and `putMaturity` > `choiceTime` (`maturity` only supplies their default). Violations are rejected with a 422 on both `/price` and `/greeks`. A supplied `mcPaths` is clamped to 2..1000000, but note the effective floor is higher: the chooser pricer runs `max(mcPaths, 20000)` paths, so any value below 20000 - including the 10000 it defaults to when omitted - executes at 20000. Analytical pricing is closed-form for both chooser types, at any pair of leg maturities, and never simulates. Monte Carlo pricing is deterministic: `rngSeed` (also accepted as `seed` or `mcSeed`) defaults to 1337, and repeating a request returns the same price. It must be an integer with `|seed| < 2^52`; fractional, non-numeric, and array/boolean/object values return a 422, and a numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer (`"1337"` yes, `"1.5"` no). Unlike `mc`, `compound` and `multiasset`, a seed of **0 is accepted** here: this engine tests for `undefined`/`null` rather than falsiness and its Mulberry32 generator adds a constant before first use, so state 0 is a working stream rather than a silent fallback to the wall clock. The generator reduces the seed with `seed >>> 0`, so seeds differing by a multiple of 2^32 are the same seed. On `/v1/compute/greeks` the seed is reused across every bumped evaluation and the same resolved seed is used by the optional insight repricer, so both remain deterministic and the Greeks measure the bump rather than sampling noise.
- **multiasset:** `payoffType` / `type` / `multiAssetType` (basket | spread | max | min), `numAssets`, `correlation`, `corrMatrix` / `correlationMatrix`, `prices[]`, `volatilities[]`, `dividends[]`, `weights[]`, `method`, `mcPaths`, `seed`, `useAntithetic`, `useControlVariate`, `useSobol`. If `prices[]` is omitted, the request spot `S` is used as the first asset price. Monte Carlo pricing is deterministic: `seed` defaults to 1337, and repeating a request returns the same price. `seed` must be an integer whose unsigned 32-bit value is non-zero - the generator is seeded with `seed >>> 0`, so 0 and any multiple of 2^32 are rejected with a 422, as are non-integer, non-numeric, and out-of-range values at or above 2^52. A numeric string is accepted only when it spells a plain integer: `"1337"` yes, `"1.0000000000000001"` no. One limit no server-side check can close: a JSON number literal is rounded to a double by the parser before it reaches the API, so a fraction finer than the double spacing at your magnitude is already gone - `1.0000000000000001` arrives as `1`. That is why the 2^52 bound exists (at and above it the spacing reaches 1, so a fractional literal has already become an integer) and why the string form is the exact one at every magnitude. The remaining numeric knobs do normalize rather than reject: `mcPaths` is clamped to 1..1000000 and defaults to 100000. `numAssets` resolves to the LARGEST of the explicit value (truncated toward zero, or 2 when omitted) and the lengths of any supplied `prices[]` / `volatilities[]` / `dividends[]` / `weights[]`, capped at 32 - so `numAssets: 2` with three prices resolves to three assets, and an omitted count with a single price still resolves to two. Each of those arrays is then padded or truncated to the resolved count using the request `S` / `sigma` / `q` and equal weights.

422.description: Semantic validation failed after request parsing/resolution. For mc, MC_PRICE_UNRESOLVED means the sampled base price plus three standard errors misses its European lower bound beyond the spot-relative tolerance. For localvol or an mc Dupire process, LOCAL_VOL_FIT_FAILED means a supplied local-vol surface or selected fit could not be used; the response carries its reason and diagnostics. For barrier, INVALID_BARRIER_MONITORING means a barrier monitoring mode, discrete frequency or date schedule is invalid or unsupported. 502.description: The broker refused the request itself (BROKER_REJECTED): an HTTP 4xx other than 408, 409, 425 and 429 that no retry fixes

503.description: Service unavailable — worker pool draining, broker connection failed, a market input's stored data could not be read (UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE, retryable, naming it in unreadFields), or the default exposure methodology could not be read for a request that named none (DEFAULT_METHODOLOGY_UNAVAILABLE, retryable)

post.description:
Compute all 17 Greeks for any of the 17 supported pricing models. Returns price alongside the full Greek vector. Accepts the same `modelParams` as `/v1/compute/price`, including ticker auto-fill (`symbol`, `expiry`, `modelParams.tickers`, `resolve.calibration`). For American-exercise Greeks on a dividend payer, use `model: "binomial"` with `isAmerican: true` and a discrete-dividend schedule - either `modelParams.dividends` (a list of `{ time: years-to-ex-date, amount: cash-per-share }`) or the webapp-style `useDiscreteDividends` / `exDividendDates` / `dividendAmounts` aliases - exactly as documented under `/v1/compute/price`. Set `includeInsight: true` to attach the Strategy-page exotic insight card for supported exotic models (Barrier, Asian, Lookback, Digital, Compound, Chooser, MultiAsset).

**Time Greeks are what one day of time passing does.** `theta`, `charm`, `color` and `veta` report the change in the price, delta, gamma and vega as one day passes, and `dcharmDvol` the change in that daily `charm` per unit of volatility, which is what one day of time passing does to `vanna` (each per `dayCount` day), and the response names that convention in `greekTimeConvention: "time-passing"`. A long option losing time value has a negative `theta`; an at-the-money long option whose gamma builds into expiry has a positive `color`.

**Breaking change (2026-10-13):** `charm`, `color`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` changed sign. Responses before it published those four against the time remaining to expiry (the opposite sign) and carried no `greekTimeConvention`; negate an earlier value to compare it with a current one. Their units and `theta` are unchanged. The same change applies to the points of `/v1/compute/sensitivity`, the legs and `netGreeks` of `/v1/compute/strategy`, and the `greeks` of `/v1/compute/price`.

**Accuracy change (2026-10-13):** `dcharmDvol` from the Black-Scholes formula is exact: the closed-form `charm` differentiated in volatility, where it had been a central difference of 0.001 in volatility. On a sampled grid (a 4% rate, a 2% dividend yield, spots from 50 to 150 against a strike of 100, tenors from a day to two years), the largest change was 0.07% of the largest value at the same volatility and tenor at 5% volatility, 0.02% at 10% and less above; relative to the value itself it was larger where the value is small, far from the money and near the spots where it changes sign. This applies to `model: "bs"`, to `model: "pde"` wherever it returns the analytical Greeks, and to the Black-Scholes Greeks of the `/v1/compute/sensitivity` points and `/v1/compute/strategy` legs. Its sign, its units and every other Greek are unchanged.

**Required tenor:** every request must specify a time-to-expiry via either `t` (numeric years) or `expiry` / `expiration` (YYYY-MM-DD). Missing both returns a `400` validation error — the API never invents a tenor.

post.description:
Generate a 2D scenario matrix of option prices across spot and volatility perturbations. Useful for risk scenario analysis and heat maps.

**Models:** defaults to `bs` (European Black-Scholes). Set `model: "binomial"` to price every cell on the ex-dividend binomial tree, honoring `isAmerican`, `steps`, `treeType`, and a discrete-dividend schedule in `modelParams` (see `/v1/compute/price`) - so an American option on a dividend payer reflects early exercise. The matrix's trees share one request's lattice allowance (see the binomial notes on `/v1/compute/price`): the tree that would pass it is refused before it is built with a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (a 20 by 20 matrix at 2000 steps is refused, one at 1000 steps fits). The response echoes the `model` used.

post.description:
Compute Greeks across a single axis (spot, time, or volatility). Returns arrays of `{ x, ...Greeks }` points suitable for charting: the 17 Greeks (filterable with `greeks`) under `bs` and `heston`, `price`, `delta` and `gamma` under `binomial`. The time Greeks are what one day of time passing does, as on `/v1/compute/greeks` (see `greekTimeConvention`).

**Supported models:** `bs` (default), `heston`, and `binomial`.

**`binomial` prices each point on the ex-dividend binomial tree**, honoring `isAmerican`, `steps`, `treeType`, and a discrete-dividend schedule in `modelParams` (see `/v1/compute/price`), so an American short call on a dividend payer shows the early-exercise divergence the `bs`/`heston` sweeps cannot. Each binomial point carries `price`, `delta`, and `gamma` only (from the binomial tree — Richardson-extrapolated when the config requests it, exactly as on `/v1/compute/price` — in the same convention as the `bs` sweep); higher-order and per-day Greeks are not computed on the binomial sweep - use `bs`/`heston`, or call `/v1/compute/greeks` with `model: "binomial"` per point, when those matter.

**Heston on this endpoint requires all five parameters explicitly.** Unlike `/v1/compute/price` and `/v1/compute/greeks`, which default `v0` and `theta` from the request `sigma`, a sweep that silently fell back to defaults would be a misleading chart rather than a single misleading number - so `v0`, `kappa`, `theta`, `volOfVol` and `rho` must all be supplied under one of their accepted spellings (see the `modelParams by model` list on `/v1/compute/price`; all spellings are accepted identically here). Omitting any of them returns a `422` with `code: "MISSING_HESTON_PARAMS"` naming the missing ones. Values that are present but out of domain return a `422` with `code: "INVALID_HESTON_PARAMS"`, and values that are not numbers return `code: "INVALID_MODEL_PARAM"` - the same resolver, rules and codes the pricing endpoints use.

post.summary: Multi-leg strategy: net price, net Greeks, payoff curve
post.description:
Price a multi-leg options strategy in a single call and get its net cost, position-level net Greeks, risk metrics (max profit/loss, breakevens, profit zone, risk/reward, probability of profit), and a payoff-at-expiry curve.

Each option leg is priced through the same model dispatcher as `/v1/compute/price` and `/v1/compute/greeks` — set a per-leg `model` of `bs` (European) or `binomial` (American-aware, with `isAmerican`, `steps`, and a discrete-dividend schedule in `modelParams`). Supply `premium` on a leg to value it at an observed market premium instead of the model price; omit it to use the model. The binomial legs' trees share one request's lattice allowance (see the binomial notes on `/v1/compute/price`): the tree that would pass it is refused before it is built, and the request with it, with a 422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED` (five `LR` legs at 2000 steps fit, a sixth is refused). Stock legs use `costBasis` (per share, defaults to the shared spot) and `quantity` in shares.

Legs share the underlying `S`/`r`/`q` and, by default, `sigma`/`t`; a leg may override `sigma` and `t` for a skew or a diagonal. Net Greeks are share-equivalent: an option leg contributes `signedQty x 100 x per-contract Greek`, a stock leg contributes `signedQty` to delta, and short legs are negative — so a covered call (100 long shares, 1 short call) nets a positive but sub-100 delta. Unbounded max profit/loss are returned as null with `unbounded` flags, since JSON cannot carry Infinity.

post.description:
Estimate the expected move of the underlying using the ATM straddle method with the industry-standard 85% adjustment factor. Also returns an IV-based approximation for comparison.

**Inputs:** pass either `atmIV` / `atmIv` for the Black-Scholes straddle approximation, or pass both `atmCallPrice` and `atmPutPrice` for a market-straddle calculation without IV. If market prices and IV are both supplied, the market prices drive the expected-move calculation and IV is returned only for comparison.

**Field naming:** accepts either `atmIV` (uppercase V, canonical) **or** `atmIv` (lowercase v) for the ATM implied volatility input. `atmIv` matches the casing returned by `/v1/data/metrics/{symbol}` and `/v1/data/snapshot/{symbol}`, so you can pipe those outputs straight in. Both fields are equivalent; if both are supplied, `atmIV` wins.

**Tip:** the `/v1/data/metrics/{symbol}` response already includes `expectedMovePct` precomputed daily — reach for this endpoint only when you need a custom `atmIV` / `daysToExpiry` / `strikePrice` combination.

post.description:
Compute the implied probability distribution of the underlying at expiration. Returns BOTH the risk-neutral distribution (eSSVI + Breeden-Litzenberger with finite-difference fallback) AND a lognormal baseline, plus statistics (implied move, range bounds, fair value). Supports two modes:

- **simple**: Pre-computed strikes + IVs (no broker needed)
- **full**: BYOK broker credentials; API fetches live chain across multiple expirations and calibrates eSSVI. A broker failure answers as on `/v1/compute/calibrate` (400 `BROKER_CREDENTIAL_INVALID`, 403 `BROKER_ENTITLEMENT_MISSING`, 429 `BROKER_RATE_LIMITED`, 502 `BROKER_REJECTED`, 503 `BROKER_UNAVAILABLE`; body `BrokerError`)

### Data requirements

At least **5 strikes** are required. The Breeden-Litzenberger second difference is taken on interior points only, so N strikes yield N-2 density points and the extractor needs 3 of them. The public request validator returns 400 for fewer than 5; broker chains that prepare fewer than 5 usable strikes return 422 `INSUFFICIENT_DISTRIBUTION_DATA`.

In `mode: "simple"`, every strike must carry a positive `iv`; an unusable value is rejected rather than substituted, because that strike's call price feeds the second difference and would bend the whole published density. In `mode: "full"`, an `expiration` that is not listed for the symbol returns a 422 `UNKNOWN_EXPIRATION` rather than being silently swapped for the front month; a listed expiration after its 4:00 p.m. `America/New_York` close returns 422 `EXPIRED_EXPIRATION` rather than being repriced at a one-day floor.

When the density cannot be extracted, `riskNeutral.pdf` is empty, `riskNeutral.stats` is `null`, and `riskNeutral.fallbackReason` carries the reason. `lognormal.stats` is `null` when the chain has no usable implied volatilities to average.

### Required headers for `mode: "full"`

- **Tradier** (1 credential header) — uses a static Production Access Token:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tradier`
  - `X-Tradier-Key: <your Tradier production access token>`
- **Tastytrade** (2 credential headers) — uses OAuth 2.0 refresh-token flow. The server posts `{grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token, client_secret}` to Tastytrade's token endpoint to mint a short-lived access token, which is reused until near expiry. Both values must come from the **same Tastytrade OAuth app**:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tastytrade`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Refresh-Token: <OAuth refresh token from your Tastytrade OAuth app>`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Client-Secret: <OAuth client secret from the SAME Tastytrade OAuth app>`
- **Schwab** (3 credential headers) — per-user-app OAuth 2.0 (BYOK). Register your own Schwab app and bring its `client_id` + `client_secret` plus a `refresh_token` from the Schwab OAuth redirect. The server exchanges them (HTTP Basic auth) for a ~30-minute access token, reused until near expiry. All three must come from the **same Schwab app**:
  - `X-Broker-Type: schwab`
  - `X-Schwab-Refresh-Token: <refresh token from your Schwab OAuth app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Id: <client id of the SAME Schwab app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Secret: <client secret of the SAME Schwab app>`
- **moomoo** (1 credential header) - the API token from the moomoo card on your Account page: moomoo's read-only sign-in, sealed to your account, so it works only with API keys on the account that connected moomoo. Connecting moomoo again replaces it. moomoo serves US option quotes in real time only once the account holds assets or a US position; until then its option quotes may be delayed (about 15 minutes) with nothing in the data to say so, so a fit on such an account can use delayed prices. A market moomoo explicitly refuses answers 403 `BROKER_ENTITLEMENT_MISSING`:
  - `X-Broker-Type: moomoo`
  - `X-Moomoo-Sealed-Token: <the API token from the moomoo card>`

`mode: "simple"` requires no headers. Public.com is not accepted in these headers; see the BYOK note for where it is.

Credential sources: Tradier → https://docs.tradier.com/docs/getting-started · Tastytrade → https://developer.tastytrade.com/oauth/ · Schwab → https://developer.schwab.com/ · moomoo → the moomoo card on your Account page (https://www.optionsanalysissuite.com/account)

post.summary: Auto-calibrate model parameters from live chain data
post.description:
Fetches the live options chain from the specified broker (BYOK credentials via headers) and calibrates model parameters. Returns fitted parameters + calibration ID for reuse in `/price` and `/greeks` via the `calibrationId` field. Supports Heston, SABR, VG, JD, and Local Volatility (eSSVI multi-expiration surface).

### Required headers by broker

- **Tradier** (1 credential header) — uses a static Production Access Token:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tradier`
  - `X-Tradier-Key: <your Tradier production access token>`
- **Tastytrade** (2 credential headers) — uses OAuth 2.0 refresh-token flow. The server posts `{grant_type: "refresh_token", refresh_token, client_secret}` to `https://api.tastyworks.com/oauth/token` to mint a short-lived access token, which is reused until near expiry; separately, calibration results themselves are cached for 30 seconds. Both credential values must come from the **same Tastytrade OAuth app** — the `client_secret` identifies which app issued the refresh token, so dropping either header fails the OAuth exchange:
  - `X-Broker-Type: tastytrade`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Refresh-Token: <OAuth refresh token from your Tastytrade OAuth app>`
  - `X-Tastytrade-Client-Secret: <OAuth client secret from the SAME Tastytrade OAuth app>`
- **Schwab** (3 credential headers) — per-user-app OAuth 2.0 (BYOK). The server posts `grant_type=refresh_token` with HTTP Basic auth over `client_id:client_secret` to `https://api.schwabapi.com/v1/oauth/token` to mint a ~30-minute access token, reused until near expiry. All three values must come from the **same Schwab app**:
  - `X-Broker-Type: schwab`
  - `X-Schwab-Refresh-Token: <refresh token from your Schwab OAuth app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Id: <client id of the SAME Schwab app>`
  - `X-Schwab-Client-Secret: <client secret of the SAME Schwab app>`
- **moomoo** (1 credential header) - the API token from the moomoo card on your Account page: moomoo's read-only sign-in, sealed to your account, so it works only with API keys on the account that connected moomoo. Connecting moomoo again replaces it. moomoo serves US option quotes in real time only once the account holds assets or a US position; until then its option quotes may be delayed (about 15 minutes) with nothing in the data to say so, so a fit on such an account can use delayed prices. A market moomoo explicitly refuses answers 403 `BROKER_ENTITLEMENT_MISSING`:
  - `X-Broker-Type: moomoo`
  - `X-Moomoo-Sealed-Token: <the API token from the moomoo card>`

Public.com is not accepted in these headers; see the BYOK note. Web-app Pro users can also use Public directly in the browser.

**Market assumptions:** Supply `riskFreeRate` and `dividendYield`, or let the API resolve them from stored rate/dividend data. If either remains unresolved, the public endpoint returns 422 `RESOLUTION_FAILED`; it never substitutes `0.05` or `0`. When the stored value could not be READ (an outage, not absence) it returns 503 `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE` (retryable) naming it in `unreadFields`. A value that is SUPPLIED but not a number or a numeric string returns 422 `INVALID_MODEL_PARAM` naming the spelling you used, rather than being coerced - `true` and `""` used to calibrate at a 100% and a 0% rate respectively. The resolved assumptions are included in the short-lived calibration cache key.

**Failure semantics:** A chain with too few usable observations returns 422 `INSUFFICIENT_CALIBRATION_DATA`. A calibrator that reports fallback/default parameters, an explicit error, or no finite non-negative fit metric returns 422 `CALIBRATION_FAILED`; those parameters are not cached or returned with a fabricated zero RMSE. A broker failure is never a caller-input 422, and never the broker's own status: credentials the broker refuses return 400 `BROKER_CREDENTIAL_INVALID` (not retryable; fix the broker headers you sent), a market the broker explicitly refuses for want of a data entitlement on your account (a moomoo permission refusal) returns 403 `BROKER_ENTITLEMENT_MISSING` (not retryable; moomoo may instead serve delayed option quotes without refusing, see the moomoo headers above), a broker rate limit returns 429 `BROKER_RATE_LIMITED` with `retryAfterSeconds` and the same wait in the `Retry-After` header (null, and no header, when the broker named no wait), a request the broker refuses itself (an HTTP 4xx other than 408, 409, 425 and 429) returns 502 `BROKER_REJECTED`, and a broker that does not answer returns 503 `BROKER_UNAVAILABLE` (retryable); the last two carry `brokerFailure` and `brokerStatus`. The body is `BrokerError`, with no broker text, and the same answer comes back when auto-calibration on `/v1/compute/price` or `/v1/compute/greeks` reaches the broker.

**Input refused before anything is spent:** An unusable option is rejected ahead of the concurrency slot and the quota reservation, so a refusal costs no calibration and no broker request. A `modelParams.jdModel` / `modelParams.modelType` that is not `kou`, `merton` or `bates` returns 422 `INVALID_CALIBRATION_OPTION` naming the value you sent - it is never silently calibrated as `kou`. An `expiration` that is well-formed but not a real calendar day (`2027-02-31`, `2027-00-00`) returns 400 `INVALID_EXPIRATION`; the format is checked against the calendar, not only against `YYYY-MM-DD`.

**Quotas:** Calibrations are hard-capped at **500 per day** per user (in addition to the 120/min compute rate limit). Over-quota returns `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header and a `CalibrationQuotaError` body. The quota window resets at midnight UTC. Cached calibration responses (30-second TTL per `credentials.type + symbol + model + expiration + modelParams + market assumptions` key) still count against the quota.

get.description:
Quarterly earnings history, EPS and revenue surprises, and next earnings date. Sourced from `earnings_data` table.

**Options analytics (`?includeOptionsAnalytics=true`)** — attach an `optionsAnalytics` block containing realized vs implied post-earnings moves, IV crush, and aggregate stats across the last 8 quarters. Derived by joining the earnings history with `stock_prices` (close-to-close realized move) and `scan_tickers` (historical ATM IV, tenor preference 7D → 30D → generic). Adds ~2 extra database reads; the base response is unchanged when the flag is false or absent.

**Windowing:** BMO (before-open) reports use prior-day close → report-day close. AMC or unknown-timing reports use report-day close → next-trading-day close. The response `quarters[].time` echoes the source `time` tag when available (currently often `null`, which falls through to AMC-style windowing).

**`impliedMovePct`** is a 1-trading-day approximation: `preEventAtmIv × √(1/252) × 100`. Event vol concentrates in the event-week expiration, so this often understates what options actually priced in; use it as a lower bound. `realizedOverImplied > 1` means the stock moved more than options priced in. `ivCrushPct` is `(preIv − postIv) / preIv × 100`.

parameters.name: includeOptionsAnalytics
parameters.description: When `true`, attach `optionsAnalytics` with per-quarter realized/implied move, IV crush, and aggregate stats (last 8 reported quarters).

priceHistory.description: The daily close history the realized moves were computed from. `unconfirmed` is true when that history is not yet confirmed by a refresh: the symbol has a split due (`pending_split`), its price history is held for review (`held`), its state could not be read (`null`; the moves are still computed), it has no closes in the window (`null`; no moves are computed then), or any close in the window is unconfirmed. Index, future and crypto symbols (`not_applicable`) are never flagged when they have closes.

upPct.description: Share of quarters with non-negative close-to-close move.

time.description: Report timing if the source tagged it; unknown/unrecognized values are normalized to null (falls through to AMC-style windowing).

preEventAtmIv.description: Decimal IV at pre-event close (e.g. 0.42 for 42%).

ivTenorUsed.description: Which IV tenor satisfied the pre-event lookup.

ivCrushTenorUsed.description: The single fixed-maturity tenor BOTH legs of `ivCrushPct` were read from. May differ from `ivTenorUsed`: the pre- and post-event rows are each resolved at their own best tenor for `preEventAtmIv`/`impliedMovePct`, but the crush requires one tenor present in both. Deliberately excludes `generic`, which is a `30d ?? 7d ?? nearest` fallback rather than a fixed maturity, so two rows carrying it may still be different tenors. Null when the rows share no fixed tenor, in which case `ivCrushPct` is null rather than comparing across maturities.

Model-specific calibration options. Supported keys by model:

**heston:** `accuracyMode` ("fast" | "balanced" | "precise", default "balanced")

**sabr:** `fixBeta` (boolean, default true), `accuracyMode` ("fast" | "balanced" | "precise")

**jd:** `modelType` / `jdModel` ("kou" | "merton" | "bates", default "kou")

The IV RMSE measures the selected fit at its usable normalized nodes. A large node residual or unidentified sparse-slice smile is reported in `warnings`; the default retains constrained slices. Saved params deterministically refit the supplied observations when priced.
