ciHigh.description: Upper bound of the 95% confidence interval for the price.

nPaths.description: Effective number of paths the estimate was built from. With antithetic variates enabled this is up to 2× the requested `nPaths`.

McDistribution.description: Terminal underlying-price distribution from a Monte Carlo simulation. Present only when `model: "mc"` and `detail: "distribution"` (or `"full"`). Computed from every simulated path — does not subsample.

count.description: Number of simulated paths the distribution was built from.

mean.description: Mean of the simulated terminal price.

percentiles.description: Linearly-interpolated percentiles of the simulated terminal price.

histogram.description: Equal-width histogram. `binEdges` length is `counts.length + 1`; bin `i` covers `[binEdges[i], binEdges[i+1])`. Bin count is configurable up to a server-enforced cap of 200; default 50.

warnings.description: Pricing approximation notices, including discrete barrier BGK monitoring.

GreeksResponse.description: Full 17-Greek response for all 17 pricing models. Analytical or native Greeks are used where available; finite-difference bump-and-reprice fills the remaining sensitivities. Monte Carlo Greeks use parallel bump-and-reprice over price-only Monte Carlo evaluations. Exotic models may optionally include an `exoticInsight` block when `includeInsight: true` is requested.

theta.description: Price change from one day of time passing: dP/dt with t the valuation date (minus dP/dT with T the time to expiry), per day - see `dayCount`. Negative for a long option losing time value.

charm.description: Delta change from one day of time passing: d²P/dSdt (minus d²P/dSdT), PER DAY - see `dayCount`. Published on the opposite sign before 2026-10-13 - see `greekTimeConvention`.

veta.description: Vega change (vega per 1% vol) from one day of time passing: d²P/dσdt (minus d²P/dσdT), per 1% vol change PER DAY - see `dayCount`. Published on the opposite sign before 2026-10-13 - see `greekTimeConvention`.

color.description: Gamma change from one day of time passing: d³P/dS²dt (minus d³P/dS²dT), PER DAY - see `dayCount`. Published on the opposite sign before 2026-10-13 - see `greekTimeConvention`.

dcharmDvol.description: Change in `charm` (the delta change from one day of time passing) per unit of volatility: d³P/dSdσdt (minus d³P/dSdσdT), PER DAY - see `dayCount`. Per unit of volatility (sigma moving by 1.00), not per 1%: one vol point moves `charm` by a hundredth of it. Published on the opposite sign before 2026-10-13 - see `greekTimeConvention`.

lambda.description: Leverage: delta × S / P (also called Omega)

phi.description: Carry-rate sensitivity. For Black-Scholes this equals rho - epsilon; exotic/numerical models may compute it independently.

greekTimeConvention.description: The sign of the five per-day time Greeks: `time-passing` means `theta`, `charm`, `color` and `veta` are what one day of time passing does to the price, delta, gamma and vega, and `dcharmDvol` is that daily `charm` differentiated by volatility, which is what one day of time passing does to `vanna`; each per `dayCount` day. Sent on every response since 2026-10-13. A response without it predates that change and carries `charm`, `color`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` on the opposite sign (their derivative against the time remaining to expiry); negate those four to compare it. Its `theta` was already time-passing.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices about this response, including ticker auto-fill, numerical-accuracy limitations or analytical fallback, and the Greek convention layer reporting a non-finite Greek that was published as 0.

ExposureStrike.description: Per-strike Greek-exposure row. Dealer-perspective dollar exposures across the full chain. Charm (`callCharm`, `putCharm`, `netCharm`) is dollar charm per calendar day on the remaining-maturity sign for the dealer, the opposite of the time-passing `charm` of `/v1/compute/greeks`: one day of time passing moves the dollar delta of the dealers by minus it.

ExposureSnapshot.description: Compact exposure summary: net totals, walls, gamma flip, abs gamma anchor, regime, top-10 strikes.

netCharm.description: Net dealer dollar charm per calendar day on the remaining-maturity sign for the dealer, the opposite of the time-passing `charm` of `/v1/compute/greeks`: one day of time passing moves the dollar delta of the dealers by minus `netCharm`.

absGamma.description: Strike with the largest absolute net gamma in the wall/flip universe

topStrikes.description: Top-10 strikes by absolute net gamma

methodologySource.description: request: the methodology the request named. default: the service's central default, as read for this request.

methodologyStale.description: Present only when the default could not be re-read and its last good value was used.

ExposureFullResult.description: Full result: compact snapshot plus the entire by-strike Greek-exposure array.

methodologySource.description: request: the methodology the request named. default: the service's central default, as read for this request.

methodologyStale.description: Present only when the default could not be re-read and its last good value was used.

ExposureResponse.description: Methodology 1: ExposureFullResult ({ snapshot, byStrike }) by default, ExposureSnapshot directly with ?detail=snapshot. Methodology 2: ExposureResponseV2 ({ methodology: 2, exposureV2 }).

ScenarioMatrixEntry.description: One cell in the scenario matrix: option value and P/L at a spot and volatility perturbation.

spot.description: Scenario spot price after applying spotChange.

pnl.description: Dollar P/L versus the base option price.

pnlPercent.description: Percent P/L versus the base option price.

model.description: Model used for the matrix. `bs` (European Black-Scholes) unless `model: "binomial"` was requested.

matrix.description: 2D matrix of structured cells indexed by [spotChange][volChange].

SensitivityResponse.description: Per-axis sweep of Greeks. Each point carries the full 17-Greek set under Black-Scholes (model defaults to "bs"). When `model: "heston"`, points additionally carry a `modelGreeks` block with derivatives w.r.t. the Heston parameters (V0, kappa, theta, volOfVol, rho); a point whose Heston price or model derivatives cannot be computed rejects the sweep (422 `NON_FINITE_RESULT`), and so does the Fourier integration panel that would take the sweep past 8 million integrand evaluations, refused before it runs (422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`), so a rejected sweep has spent at most 8 million. When `model: "binomial"`, each point carries `price`, `delta`, and `gamma` only, and the sweep's trees share one request's lattice allowance (see the binomial notes on `/v1/compute/price`): the tree that would pass it is refused before it is built (422 `COMPUTE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`).

greekTimeConvention.description: The sign of the time Greeks on every point: what one day of time passing does, per `dayCount` day, as on `/v1/compute/greeks` (see its `greekTimeConvention`). A sweep without it predates 2026-10-13 and carries `charm`, `color`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` on the opposite sign.

SensitivityPoint.description: One point on a sensitivity sweep. `x` is the sweep variable (spot price for axis="spot", days-to-expiry for "time", volatility for "volatility"). The standard 17 Greeks come from Black-Scholes; `modelGreeks` is present only when `model: "heston"`. Under `model: "binomial"` only `price`, `delta`, and `gamma` are populated.

x.description: Sweep variable value at this point.

theta.description: Price change from one day of time passing, per `dayCount` day (as `GreeksResponse.theta`).

charm.description: Delta change from one day of time passing, per `dayCount` day (as `GreeksResponse.charm`).

veta.description: Vega (per 1% vol) change from one day of time passing, per `dayCount` day (as `GreeksResponse.veta`).

color.description: Gamma change from one day of time passing, per `dayCount` day (as `GreeksResponse.color`).

dcharmDvol.description: Change in `charm` per unit of volatility, per `dayCount` day (as `GreeksResponse.dcharmDvol`).

HestonModelGreeks.description: Sensitivities of the Heston price to its five model parameters. Present only when `model: "heston"` was requested. Computed by symmetric finite-difference around the calibrated parameter point; useful for assessing exposure to a miscalibrated Heston model (vs. classic Greeks which assume the model is correct and only the market inputs vary).

dV0.description: d(price) / d(V0) — sensitivity to instantaneous variance.

StrategyLeg.description: One priced leg of the strategy. Option legs carry `strike`, `model`, and `premium` (per share); stock legs carry `costBasis` (per share). `greeks` are per-contract for options and `{ delta: 1 }` for stock.

premium.description: Per-share option premium used — supplied by the caller or computed by the model.

costBasis.description: Per-share cost basis for a stock leg (defaults to the shared spot).

greeks.description: Per-contract Greeks for option legs, in the `/v1/compute/greeks` convention with the per-day Greeks per calendar day (365): `theta`, `charm`, `color`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` are what one day of time passing does (see `greekTimeConvention`). `{ delta: 1 }` for stock.

retainedGreeks.description: Only Greeks that retain a native or earlier completed estimate after an optional accuracy fit could not finish. Omitted when none do, including stock legs. Legs share one request allowance, so a leg can receive a fit alone and retain an estimate in a larger strategy. This labels the affected estimate without certifying its accuracy.

type.description: One of: above, below, between, outside, always_profit, always_loss, complex, unknown.

profitIntervals.description: Profitable price bands [lo, hi] for disjoint (complex) zones. A null endpoint means unbounded on that side (0 low / +inf high).

payoff.description: Total P&L at expiry at this price (intrinsic payoff plus the initial cost).

StrategyResponse.description: Net cost, position-level net Greeks, risk metrics, and a payoff-at-expiry curve for a multi-leg strategy. Unbounded profit/loss and an unbounded risk/reward ratio are reported as null (JSON has no Infinity); the `unbounded` flags say which.

initialCost.description: Net cash flow to establish the position: negative = net debit paid, positive = net credit received. Options are x100/contract; stock is x shares.

netGreeks.description: Position-level (share-equivalent) net Greeks: an option leg contributes signedQty x 100 x per-contract Greek; a stock leg contributes signedQty to delta. Short legs are negative. Excludes `lambda` (leverage is a ratio, not additive) — see each leg`s `greeks` for its lambda.

maxProfit.description: Maximum profit, or null when unbounded (see `unbounded.maxProfit`).

maxLoss.description: Maximum loss (most negative P&L), or null when unbounded.

riskRewardRatio.description: maxProfit / |maxLoss|; null when maxLoss is 0 or unbounded.

probabilityOfProfit.description: Lognormal probability of finishing in a profit zone; null unless sigma and tenor are known.

greekTimeConvention.description: The sign of the time Greeks in each leg and in `netGreeks`: what one day of time passing does, per calendar day, as on `/v1/compute/greeks` (see its `greekTimeConvention`). A response without it predates 2026-10-13 and carries `charm`, `color`, `veta` and `dcharmDvol` on the opposite sign.

warnings.description: A conditional notice when optional binomial accuracy fits cannot finish. Each affected leg identifies its retained estimates in retainedGreeks; fewer steps or fewer legs leave more allowance for fits.

method.description: essvi uses the calibrated constrained-slice surface and reports large node residuals in warnings; finite-diff uses the chain-price fallback.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices about the fitted surface used for this distribution, including large eSSVI node residuals and sparse maturities whose smile shape is borrowed.

ivRmse.description: Aggregate IV RMSE across the options the fit was computed from. For Heston, an option priced inside its bid/ask counts zero and one outside counts its IV distance to the nearer side, relative to its market IV, so a fit that prices every option inside its quote reports 0. A calibration that does not converge returns a 422 `CALIBRATION_FAILED` rather than an `ivRmse` of 0 next to unfitted parameters.

nOptions.description: Number of usable observations admitted by the selected calibrator. This can differ from the submitted chain count: Heston requires a supplied IV in its accepted range; SABR, variance-gamma and jump-diffusion can derive IV from a usable option price; and local-vol/eSSVI deduplicates call/put observations at the same expiry and strike.

warnings.description: Non-fatal notices about the calibrated surface, including large eSSVI node residuals and sparse maturities whose smile shape is borrowed.

FitDiagnostics.description: Per-moneyness-bucket fit-quality diagnostics. Computed by re-pricing each market option with the calibrated parameters. Currently emitted for `model: "heston"` only; other models will gain support as their public price functions are exposed.

residuals.description: Per-option residuals (model price − market mid). Capped at 100, sorted by descending |residual| so the worst fits survive the cap.

bucketRmse.description: RMSE of price residuals within each moneyness bucket. Null when the bucket has no eligible options.

bucketCount.description: Number of options included in each moneyness bucket, mirrors `bucketRmse`.

worstFitOption.description: Single worst-fitting option in absolute residual terms. Null if no options were re-priceable.

moneyness.description: K / S at the time of calibration.

priceResidual.description: Model price − market mid (in price units, NOT IV units — aggregate `fitError.ivRmse` is the IV-space companion).

RegimeResponse.description: Latest market regime. Both `daily` and `intraday` are raw rows from the regime_daily / regime_intraday warehouse tables. Field set is owned by the data-pipeline team and may evolve over time — access defensively. Either field may be null when no row is available. A row's `vector._meta` carries its two Greek exposure blocks, `gex` (methodology 1) and `gexV2` (methodology 2): see RegimeExposureMeta.

daily.description: Latest row from regime_daily for symbol=MARKET, scope=market, ordered by market_date desc. Null when no row exists.

intraday.description: Latest row from regime_intraday for symbol=MARKET, scope=market, ordered by (market_date, scan_time) desc. Null when no row exists.

MaxPainCurveRow.description: One per-strike row of the max-pain curve. Pain values are dollar-weighted aggregate OI × distance × multiplier.

SnapshotResponse.description: EOD options snapshot: spot, IV term structure, GEX/DEX/HV, max pain, plus opaque curve payloads consumed by the web app charts. netGex, netDex and the *ByStrike curves are methodology 1 (legacy); exposureV2 carries methodology 2 beside them.

maxPainCurve.description: Max-pain curve series for the chart UI: per-strike rows of { strike, callPain, putPain, totalPain }.

gexByStrike.description: Per-strike rows of { strike, callGex, putGex, netGex }. The legs are ABSOLUTE values and netGex is the signed sum of the underlying signed legs, so it is NOT recoverable from the two shown without knowing their signs. Dealer call gamma is positive and put gamma negative, which makes netGex = callGex - putGex. Source of truth: packages/shared/src/exposure-compute.ts.

dexByStrike.description: Per-strike rows of { strike, callDex, putDex, netDex }. The legs are ABSOLUTE values and netDex is the signed sum of the underlying signed legs. Delta exposure signs run OPPOSITE to gamma: the call leg is negative and the put leg positive, so netDex = putDex - callDex and a negative netDex means the call leg is the larger one. Source of truth: packages/shared/src/exposure-compute.ts.

vannaByStrike.description: Per-strike rows of { strike, callVanna, putVanna, netVanna }. The legs are ABSOLUTE values and netVanna is the signed sum of the underlying signed legs, which here share a sign, so the magnitude of netVanna is callVanna + putVanna. Source of truth: packages/shared/src/exposure-compute.ts.

charmByStrike.description: Per-strike rows of { strike, callCharm, putCharm, netCharm }. The legs are ABSOLUTE values and netCharm is the signed sum of the underlying signed legs, dealer dollar charm per calendar day on the remaining-maturity sign for the dealer, the opposite of the time-passing `charm` of `/v1/compute/greeks`: one day of time passing moves the dollar delta of the dealers by minus `netCharm`. Unlike vanna and vomma, the call and put charm legs are computed from DIFFERENT expressions and do not necessarily share a sign, so netCharm is not recoverable from the two shown. Source of truth: packages/shared/src/exposure-compute.ts.

vommaByStrike.description: Per-strike rows of { strike, callVomma, putVomma, netVomma }. The legs are ABSOLUTE values and netVomma is the signed sum of the underlying signed legs, which here share a sign, so the magnitude of netVomma is callVomma + putVomma. Source of truth: packages/shared/src/exposure-compute.ts.

volSkew.description: Vol-skew curve KEYED BY EXPIRATION: { "YYYY-MM-DD": [{ strike, iv }] }, each list sorted by strike. It is not a pair of parallel strike/iv arrays. Source of truth: proxy/services/SnapshotComputeService.ts:1023.

chainData.description: Recent option chain rows; opaque payload

exposureV2.description: Methodology 2 beside the legacy fields, never inside them.

EodExposureResponse.description: Compact end-of-day dealer-positioning levels for one symbol. The legacy fields (methodology 1) are computed over a single 0-60 DTE universe so every one agrees: gamma magnet, gamma flip, call/put walls, dealer regime, net GEX/DEX, 30-day expected move, and the top strikes by gamma contribution; the window, units, and schemaVersion travel with every row. exposureV2 carries methodology 2 beside them, over every expiration after the date. Returns 404 when no usable EOD option data exists for the symbol/date (e.g. thinly-traded names or futures symbols, which are not covered), whatever its methodology-2 book.

schemaVersion.description: Contract version; bumped on any breaking shape change.

date.description: EOD session the levels are computed from.

asOf.description: When the pipeline computed this row.

dteWindow.description: Expiration window every level is computed over.

netGex.description: Net dollar gamma exposure over the window (see units).

netDex.description: Net dollar delta exposure over the window (see units).

gammaMagnet.description: Strike with the largest absolute net gamma in the window.

dealerRegime.description: Sign of net gamma at spot over the window.

expectedMovePct30d.description: 30-day ATM-implied move as a decimal fraction.

topContributingStrikes.description: Strikes contributing most to net gamma, ordered by absolute gamma contribution.

topContributingStrikesLimit.description: Max number of rows returned in topContributingStrikes.

units.description: Plain-language units for the exposure and expected-move fields.

exposureV2.description: Methodology 2 beside the legacy fields, never inside them.

MetricsResponse.description: Per-symbol EOD metrics row. Sourced from option_ticker_snapshots.

IVSurfaceResponse.description: Strike × expiration grid of implied volatility for the symbol. Each row carries the smoothed value (`smv`), the call-side and put-side mid IVs, and a unified `iv` that falls back through smv → callIV → putIV. Any of the IV fields may be null when source data is missing.

ticker.description: Underlying symbol echoed from the request (uppercased).

date.description: Market date the surface snapshot applies to.

spotPrice.description: Spot price observed for this surface, in dollars.

expirations.description: Sorted list of distinct expiration dates present in `data`.

rowCount.description: Number of strike × expiration rows returned.

yte.description: Years to expiration as a decimal (calendar-day fraction).

iv.description: Unified IV — smv → callIV → putIV fallback. Null only if all three sources are missing.

atm_iv_7d.description: 7-day tenor ATM IV — closest persisted proxy to event-week vol around earnings.

workerPool.description: Current compute-worker capacity. Null means heavy computations have no worker pool and may use their documented fallback path.

redis.description: Redis connectivity. When Redis is down, the rate limiter and concurrency caps fall back to per-process memory and stop being global across replicas; response caching is bypassed.

rejections.description: Per-process refusal counters since startup. The path breakdown is capped; overflowed=true means totals remain complete but byBucket is partial.

CalibrationQuotaError.description: Returned by /v1/compute/calibrate when the user exceeds the per-day calibration cap. Separate from the general rate limit — calibrations are hard-capped because each run can consume 5-60 seconds of CPU.

limit.description: Hard cap for the scope (500 per day)

used.description: Number of successful calibrations the user has made in the scope window

resetsAt.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the quota window resets (UTC)

message.example: Heston sensitivity requires v0, kappa, theta, xi/volOfVol, and rho

missingFields.description: Fields that ticker resolution could not fill, present on RESOLUTION_FAILED responses

unreadFields.description: The missing fields whose stored data could not be READ (an outage, not absence), present on 503 UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE responses: a retry may resolve them

warnings.description: Non-fatal resolver warnings, present when ticker auto-fill ran

partialResolved.description: Resolved market inputs available before the semantic validation failure

error.example: No data found for this symbol

retryable.description: Present on UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE: true, a retry may succeed

missingFields.description: UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE: every market input the request still needs (the unread ones and any with nothing on file)

unreadFields.description: UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE: the missing inputs whose stored data could not be read (an outage, not absence)

BrokerError.description: A failure of the broker read made with your broker credentials (data-api lib/brokerReads.ts), answered as the live broker routes answer it and never with the broker's own status. No broker text is returned. A broker that explicitly refuses a market for want of a data entitlement on your account (a moomoo permission refusal) answers 403 BROKER_ENTITLEMENT_MISSING, not retryable. moomoo may instead serve delayed option quotes, unmarked, to an account without real-time option permission, so the absence of this error does not mean the data is real-time.

retryable.description: Whether the same request can succeed later. False for a refused credential or a refused request.

message.description: What to do next (BROKER_CREDENTIAL_INVALID, BROKER_RATE_LIMITED, BROKER_ENTITLEMENT_MISSING).

retryAfterSeconds.description: BROKER_RATE_LIMITED: the wait the broker named, null when it named none.

brokerFailure.description: BROKER_REJECTED and BROKER_UNAVAILABLE: what kind of failure it was.

brokerStatus.description: BROKER_REJECTED and BROKER_UNAVAILABLE: the broker's HTTP status, null when it gave none.

RegimeExposureStrikeAvailability.description: Which of a regime top strike's Greeks its rows carried (from 2026-07-20).

RegimeExposureStrike.description: One of a regime row's top strikes: the ExposureStrike fields, with which Greeks its rows carried.

RegimeExposureAvailability.description: How many rows each Greek counted in a regime row's methodology 1 block (from 2026-07-20): gamma, delta, vega, and the higher-order Greeks (vanna, charm, vomma).

RegimeExposureV1.description: A regime row's methodology 1 (legacy) block, `vector._meta.gex`: the ExposureSnapshot fields over the row's chain, with how many rows each Greek counted. Rows written before 2026-05-04 lack absGamma, before 2026-07-20 availability, before 2026-10-12 methodology.

netCharm.description: Net dealer dollar charm per calendar day on the remaining-maturity sign for the dealer, the opposite of the time-passing `charm` of `/v1/compute/greeks`: one day of time passing moves the dollar delta of the dealers by minus `netCharm`.

absGamma.description: Strike with the largest absolute net gamma in the wall/flip universe

topStrikes.description: Top-10 strikes by absolute net gamma

ApiKeyAuth.description: API key authentication. Pass via `Authorization: Bearer oas_live_...` or `X-API-Key` header.

ApiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
ApiKeyHeader.description: Alternative: pass API key via `X-API-Key` header instead of `Authorization`.
